land.text: the Croat-majority municipalities of Herzegovina and western and central Bosnia (1991 census: 1,238,512 people in the claimed territory, 44.91% Croats)

predecessors.note: Cliopatria's Yugoslavia row ends 1991; the Bosnian dossier opens in March 1992.

land.text: the Croat-held land 'to be joined with Bosniaks into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina' under the Washington Agreement of March 1994

successors.note: The page says Herzeg-Bosnia was formally abolished only in August 1996 (agreed 14 August); the dossier ends with the land, in March 1994, as the Bosnian dossier's gain does.

capitals.name: Mostar
capitals.note: 'Its capital city was Mostar, which was then a war zone, and the effective control center was in Grude' (Grude lies about 17.2 E, 43.37 N). Coordinates are Mostar's.

rulers.name: Mate Boban, president
rulers.title: President
rulers.note: 'Mate Boban led the entity from 1991 to 1994, followed by Krešimir Zubak (1994-1996)'; Jadranko Prlić was prime minister 1993-1996.

correction.text: the Croat-held land of Herzegovina around Mostar and the western cantons, 12,937 km2 in 1995 per the infobox; 'at its proclaimed borders the entity covered about 30% of the country but never fully controlled that area'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page lists no municipalities; the three Natural Earth units (Herzegovina-Neretva, West Herzegovina, West Bosnia; about 11,100 km2 at the grid) follow the Bosnian dossier's contest zone and sit within 14% of the infobox figure. The proclaimed 30% of the country would be larger; central Bosnian territory (the Lašva Valley) passed to the Bosnian government in early 1993 and is not drawn.

region.text: the Croat-held land of Herzegovina and western Bosnia

ledger.note: 18 November 1991: the Croatian Community of Herzeg-Bosnia is proclaimed. 'It was proclaimed on 18 November 1991 under the name Croatian Community of Herzeg-Bosnia', with Mate Boban as president; local party leaders had agreed a policy toward a common Croatian state on 12 November 1991. The page lists no municipalities, so the region is the Bosnian dossier's reading.

region.text: Herzegovina around Mostar and the western cantons

ledger.note: October 1992: the Croat-Bosniak War begins. The infobox dates the war to 18 October 1992; 'in early 1993 the Croat-Bosniak War escalated' and within two months most of central Bosnia was under Bosnian government control. The 21 July 1992 Agreement on Friendship and Cooperation had set up Bosnian-Croatian military cooperation.

28 August 1993: Herzeg-Bosnia is declared a republic. 'On 28 August 1993, Herzeg-Bosnia was declared a republic' at Grude, under the Owen-Stoltenberg proposal; the Bosnian government did not recognise it.

region.text: Herzegovina around Mostar and the western cantons

ledger.note: March 1994: the Washington Agreement ends the Croat-Bosniak war. 'In March 1994, the Washington Agreement was signed that ended the conflict between Croats and Bosniaks'; the ceasefire was signed on 18 March 1994 with a ceremony hosted by Bill Clinton.

region.text: the Croat-held land, to the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina

ledger.note: March 1994: Herzeg-Bosnia's land is joined to the Federation. 'Under the agreement, Herzeg-Bosnia was to be joined with Bosniaks into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina' (ten cantons); the page adds that the Federation 'largely failed to function' and that on 14 August 1996 it was agreed that Herzeg-Bosnia would be formally abolished by the end of that month. The dossier ends with the land; the institution's last two years are in the note.

wars.name: Croat-Bosniak War

zones.text: Herzegovina around Mostar and the western cantons

wars.outcome: Ended by the Washington Agreement of March 1994 (ceasefire 18 March), which joined the Croat-held land with the Bosniak-held land into the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.
wars.note: The Bosnian War page says Bosniaks and Croats were allies against Republika Srpska after the Washington Agreement, which led to the Federation; it does not date the Agreement. The Constitutional Court of Bosnia and Herzegovina declared the proclamation unconstitutional on 14 September 1992 (both pages).

certainty.note: A claim and a front, not a border: the entity 'never fully controlled' its proclaimed territory; the page lists no municipalities.

sources.title: Croatian Republic of Herzeg-Bosnia
sources.note: Whole dossier: 18 November 1991, 28 August 1993, 12,937 km2, Mostar and Grude, Washington Agreement, abolition August 1996.

sources.title: Bosnian War
sources.note: Herzeg-Bosnia established 18 November 1991 at Mostar with Mate Boban; the Washington Agreement and the Federation.

notes: Requested as a counterpart by eu-22-e. Modelled as a rebel state for 1991-1994 so that its events mirror the Bosnian dossier's (contest_start 18 October 1992, contest_end and gain March 1994). The page puts the formal abolition at the end of August 1996 (agreed 14 August 1996, after a Dayton requirement of two weeks that the Federation failed to meet); the orchestrator may extend the dossier to 1996 if the rendering wants the parallel institution drawn, but then the Bosnian dossier's gain of March 1994 would double-count the land. Not settled: the municipalities, the central Bosnian lands held in 1992, the Posavina and Lašva pockets, Croatia's role in land (the OSCE report calling Herzeg-Bosnia 'in every respect part of Croatia' is undated on the page), the Vance-Owen provinces (the page names Owen-Stoltenberg instead). Grude is not in the gazetteer's places.
